hooks.definition: Opens on one specific number and says what it counts.
Opens on what something cost, as an amount of money, hours or attention.
Opens on one concrete thing you could point at: a form, a label, a button, a ticket.
Puts two true things side by side that should not both hold.
Opens inside one dated instant, as it happened, with no set-up.
Opens on a line someone really said or wrote, with the speaker's role.
Defines a word the way the work really uses it, not the way a dictionary does.
Opens on a plain admission of what we got wrong, in the first person.
Sets two things next to each other and lets the gap between them do the work.
Opens on a picture or drawing that carries the claim before any words do.
Opens on one result that does not fit the pattern around it.
Shows a real document, screen or file as found, with one part marked.

closes.definition: Ends on what we do differently now.
Ends by admitting what is still unsolved or not yet known.
Ends on the point, in one flat sentence with no flourish.
Returns to the object or line the piece opened on, now changed.
Ends on a small remark off to the side of the argument, said lightly.
Ends by giving the reader something to take away: a template, a check, a number to reuse.
Ends on the next thing we will test and what result would change our mind.
Ends on a picture, with no claim in a caption.
Ends on one rule short enough to repeat.
Ends by answering, in one line, the question the piece opened with.

layouts.stack: the hook in a band at the top, the object in a band under it, the proof and the source under that.
layouts.split: the page divides into two unequal fields side by side: the object fills the narrow one from top to bottom, the hook and its proof stand in the wide one.
layouts.bleed: the object is drawn larger than the page and is cut by two edges; the hook stands in the space it leaves, low on the page.
layouts.grid: a modular grid of equal cells: the object fills a block of cells top right, and the hook takes the block of cells under it on the left margin, so the eye runs on a diagonal.
layouts.table: the page is one ruled table: its rows are the object, and the hook is the last row, the total or the answer, set at display size.
layouts.map: the object spreads over the whole page and its positions mean something; the hook sits inside the map, beside the place it points at.
layouts.diagram: the object is drawn large in the upper two thirds; the hook is its caption, under it.
layouts.quote: the real words are the hook, set at display size over most of the page; the object is small, as its attribution.
layouts.number: one real number at display size leads the page (data-role number); the hook says what it counts, beside or under it.
layouts.artefact: the object as found, large and cut by one edge; the hook is its label, under it on the margin.
layouts.sequence: the object is a run of steps in reading order across the page; the hook is the last step, at the foot on the right.
layouts.field: a full colour field and the hook alone on it, low and large, with the source at the foot.
